questions.question: When Forum.post adds a record, what does its prev_hash point to?
options: The forum's current head before the new record
The author's previous result only
A random 16-character value
The SHA-256 hash of the next record
questions.explanation: post links the new record to the current head, then hashes the payload containing that predecessor link.

questions.question: How does the fixed regime differ from the free regime in solve?
options: Fixed always returns the task's base score
Fixed adds bounded random upside to the base, while free uses a wider Gaussian variation
Free clips every score to the base
Fixed lets the agent edit the forum before scoring
questions.explanation: The fixed regime uses base + random*0.25 with a bounded ceiling; free samples a wider Gaussian around a positive offset and can go down as well as up.

questions.question: What does Forum.verify report after attempt_tamper changes a stored result without rebuilding later links?
options: An empty list because result values are not hashed
Only the number of tasks
Indexes whose hash-chain records no longer recompute correctly
A new genesis record that repairs the chain
questions.explanation: verify recomputes each record's payload and predecessor link, so the changed record and any dependent links can be reported as corrupt.

questions.question: Why is the forum useful as an alignment-research artifact in this lesson?
options: It lets an agent delete an inconvenient result
It proves every score is correct
It replaces human review with a random seed
Its append-only records make provenance and later tampering inspectable
questions.explanation: The hash chain preserves an auditable sequence of authors, tasks, regimes, results, and links; it does not itself validate the scientific result.

questions.question: What is the main statistical trade-off illustrated by free versus fixed agents?
options: Free agents expose more upside and downside variance, while fixed agents stay in a narrower range
Free agents cannot solve any task
Fixed agents always outperform free agents
The two regimes produce identical distributions
questions.explanation: Free uses a wider Gaussian perturbation, whereas fixed keeps variation bounded, so the free regime has more spread around the task baseline.

questions.question: Which data contribute to Forum's my_hash for a newly posted record?
options: Only the author's name
The author, task, regime, formatted result, and previous hash
Only the random seed
The result after the next record is posted
questions.explanation: post builds a pipe-delimited payload from those fields, including the predecessor hash, and stores the first 16 hexadecimal characters of its SHA-256 digest.
